en.title: Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom Channels Iron Man in Avengers: Doomsday Trailer
en.summary: A new trailer for Marvel's Avengers: Doomsday has dropped, featuring a striking visual callback to Tony Stark's iconic debut. Robert Downey Jr. makes his anticipated return, this time as the formidable Doctor Doom.
en.body:
The multiverse is officially on notice. Marvel Studios has unleashed a new trailer for **Avengers: Doomsday**, and it’s packed with the kind of epic spectacle we’ve come to expect. But beyond the cosmic stakes and the assembly of heroes, one moment is already sparking intense discussion among fans: the chillingly familiar pose struck by **Robert Downey Jr.**’s Doctor Doom.

In the footage, which appears to be the same special look debuted at San Diego Comic-Con, Doom, played by the returning RDJ, commands a legion of Sentinels, the formidable mutant-hunting robots now seemingly under his control. As they rise from the earth, awakened by his green-hued power, Doom turns to the camera. It's then that the visual echo hits: his stance, his commanding presence, directly mirrors Tony Stark’s iconic pose from the very first **Iron Man** film in 2008. This isn't just a subtle nod; it's a powerful statement, connecting the genesis of the MCU with its potential end.

This deliberate callback is more than just fan service; it’s narrative shorthand. While Tony Stark’s journey was fueled by trauma that turned him into a hero, Doom’s path, as hinted, is one of absolute power and perhaps a twisted sense of order. The juxtaposition is potent, suggesting that the strength of all heroes combined will be needed to face this new, terrifying threat. The trailer also offers a glimpse of **Pedro Pascal** as Reed Richards, setting the stage for a multiversal clash unlike any seen before.

## The Fan Frenzy Begins

The internet, as always, is ablaze with reactions. While many are celebrating the return of **Robert Downey Jr.** and the sheer ambition of **Avengers: Doomsday**, the Iron Man callback has become a focal point. Fans are dissecting the visual similarities, with some praising Marvel’s commitment to thematic resonance and others pointing out perceived differences in production quality between the original **Iron Man** and this new footage. Regardless of the debate, the buzz is undeniable, proving that RDJ’s presence, in any form, is still a massive draw.

## What's Next

**Avengers: Doomsday** is slated for release on December 18, 2026. With tickets already on sale for select Infinity Vision certified theaters, anticipation is building for what promises to be a universe-defining event. Keep an eye out for further trailers and casting announcements as we approach the film's release.

content_raw: Alongside a presentation at D23 last week, Marvel Studios released a new “special look” at its upcoming superhero team-up movie, Avengers: Doomsday . This appears to be the same footage the studio debuted at San Diego Comic-Con, featuring an emotional confrontation between Reed Richards (Pedro Pascal) and Doctor Doom (Robert Downey Jr.) and revealing Doom’s control over a group of Sentinels , the giant robots known to hunt the X-Men. At the end of the trailer, Doom places his hands on the ground and, through some green-hued magic, awakens the Sentinels, who seem to have been buried in the ground. As they rise up, he turns to the camera and strikes a very familiar pose that calls back to the first Iron Man film in 2008, where we first met Tony Stark (also Robert Downey Jr.) boasting about the damage his Stark Industries Jericho missiles could do for the U.S. military before he had an epiphany and decided that protecting people was a much better direction for his life to take. Tony acting the same in different universes.” The visuals of Jon Favreau’s MCU-kickstarting Iron Man certainly do feel old-school compared to Marvel ’s later output, but the transition to a heavier use of computer-generated effects didn’t harm the studio’s performance at the box office when it came to its last two Avengers films. Only time will tell if this forthcoming Avengers installment also has the juice, but anticipation is still building around Doomsday , where Steve Rogers (Chris Evans) will return to help Thor, Ant-Man, The New Avengers, the other Avengers, Black Panther, the X-Men , and the Fantastic Four stand their ground against Doom’s multiverse-clashing endgame before a follow-up film called Avengers: Secret Wars arrives in 2028 to potentially conclude the classic Marvel villain’s first arc.
